## What landed (all engineered + fixture-verified; no live leg exists)

- `connectors/src/connectors/opt_out.py` (new, ~215 lines) +
  `connectors/src/connectors/data/opt_out_register.toml`
  (`sig.opt-out-register/1`): the committed, append-only host-level
  opt-out register. Bare hosts normalize (case/scheme/port/trailing-dot)
  and cover themselves + sub-domains; every row is evidence-bearing
  (`host` + `recorded_on` + `evidence`); a malformed row fails closed.
  `load_register()` precedence: explicit path → `$SIG_OPT_OUT_REGISTER`
  (the operator-supplied file — the no-rebuild/no-redeploy "immediately"
  seam, E2-06/NEW-3) → the packaged artifact. `sig-connectors validate`
  fails on a malformed register.
- `policy/src/policy/crawler.py` — `detect_reservation()` +
  `ReservationSignal`/`ReservationVerdict` and the per-channel detectors:
  `Content-Signal` directives (`ai-train=no` and the sibling automated-use
  keys `ai-input`/`search`), `TDM-Reservation` (EU DSM Article 4 header
  form), `X-Robots-Tag` `noai`/`noimageai`, and the page-level forms on
  HTML (`<meta name="robots" content="…noai…">`,
  `<meta name="tdm-reservation">`). Signals return verbatim; absent or
  malformed signals are never refusals (and never grants). A robots
  `Disallow` is **not** a reservation — GL-GATE-08 untouched.
- `policy/src/policy/rights.py` — `RightsReservation` (frozen, validated:
  closed `RESERVATION_KINDS` vocabulary + verbatim + `observed_on` +
  evidence — asserted only on evidence, §3.1) and the additive
  `RightsRecord.reservation` field. `is_refused` is a distinct axis from
  `is_undetermined`: unresolved rights invite the Stage-0 conversation, a
  recorded reservation closes it (SIG-INGEST-046c).
- `connectors/src/connectors/net.py` — `HostOptOut` raised before ANY
  egress (before the robots probe; recorded on `opt_out_refusals`) and
  `ReservationRefused` raised on a response carrying an affirmative
  reservation (bytes never captured; verbatim signals recorded on
  `reservations`, and the message carries them for the run record).
- `connectors/src/connectors/pipeline.py` — both refusals land on
  `report.refusals` as first-class dispositions on any target (recorded
  data, never a disappearance and never a swallowed exception); the run
  continues to the next target and no claim derives from refused bytes.
- Gate wiring — `assert_loadable` refuses a source whose rights record
  carries a recorded reservation on every path; `live_gate_reasons` names
  the reservation AND an opt-out-listed source homepage host (a malformed
  register refuses, fail-closed); `review.py` `GateBreakdown.rights_reserved`
  (never flip-ready, never loadable) and `review_metadata_violations`
  flags a flipped record carrying a refusal; `review-status` prints
  `reserved=`.
- `connectors/src/connectors/registry.py` — the optional
  `[sources.<id>.rights.reservation]` sub-table parses the recorded
  refusal (fail-closed on malformed).
- Tests — `tests/connectors/test_opt_out.py` (29), extended
  `tests/unit/test_policy_crawler.py` (+11), new
  `tests/unit/test_policy_rights.py` (5): register parse/normalise/
  sub-domain/env-override/fail-closed; zero-egress opt-out refusal;
  Content-Signal/TDM/X-Robots-Tag/Article-4 meta fixtures; refused ≠
  UNDETERMINED; robots-disallow ≠ reservation (the disallow proceeds,
  stamps `robots_disregarded`, and a reservation on top refuses);
  every gate seam; run-report recording.

## Deviations

- `docs` CI failed on the first head `bd6b9d9b` — the SIG-REL-014
  changelog gate counts `policy/**` as public-behaviour paths; repaired
  with the `[Unreleased]` entry at `e6b344d7`. Recorded, not smoothed.
- A rights refusal on a seed target records on `report.refusals` and the
  run continues (rather than propagating like a politeness refusal):
  an opted-out host is recorded data, and one listed host must never
  abort a multi-tenant sweep — engineering judgment under the ticket's
  "the refusal lands in the run report" wording, not an ADR.
- The register consult happens at the shared fetcher (every egress) and
  the live gate names the source's homepage host; per-target hosts are
  covered by the per-fetch consult (the load-bearing layer).
- No new ADR — the row executes the ticket contract under ADR-168's
  ratified posture (GL-GATE-08 unchanged); no owned SHOULD-level
  decision and no contract deviation to record.
